To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we determined the stellar masses and [Fe/H] for a sample of 18 nearby open clusters.

we derived the stellar masses and metallicities of 18 giant star members of six nearby open clusters, which will allow us to disentangle mass and metallicity effects in a search for planets around giants.
the metallicity range of the 18 clusters is between −0.2 and +0.2 dex, with the mean metallicity of −0.03 ± 0.05 dex, and that the 18 open clusters cover a mass range from 0.8 to 3.0 solar masses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the stellar and cluster parameters of the 18 clusters in order to obtain the most accurate values for the masses of the target stars.
a sample of 31 clusters, which are used to search for planets orbiting giant stars in the solar neighborhood.

the following: (1) the derivation of accurate stellar parameters and metallicities for a sample of 18 open clusters; (2) the analysis of the metallicity distribution of open clusters and its comparison to the metallicity distribution function (MDF) of the field; (3) the comparison between the MDF of open clusters and the MDF of the field in order to study the effects of the mass and metallicity on planet formation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence of a correlation between the metallicity of a star and its planet occurrence rate, neither for stars of the same mass nor for stars of the solar mass.
the frequency of planets around giants is independent of the metallicity and the mass of the stars.
there is no clear evidence of a dependence of the frequency of planets on the stellar metallicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there is a clear metallicity gradient in the solar neighbourhood with a slope of −0.08 dex/kpc, but that the metallicity distribution function is rather flat, with a peak at [Fe/H] = 0.0 dex and a dispersion of about 0.2 dex.

the metallicity distribution of open clusters in the solar neighbourhood is not a simple Gaussian, as was often thought in the past, but that there are many clusters with metallicities close to that of the Sun, but with a tail towards low and high metallicities.
we have derived stellar parameters and metallicities for 29 clusters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the metallicity range of the clusters is much larger than what was previously thought.
the metallicity distribution of open clusters is much broader than previously thought.
the metallicity of the stars in open clusters is not a good predictor of their planet occurrence.
